title: Canonical polynomial chart, base and tensor maps for extended Rees algebras
statement: Let $A$ and $R$ be commutative rings in arbitrary universes, $d\in\mathbf N$, $P=A[x_j:j\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $\psi:P\to R$ any ring map, regarded as a $P$-algebra structure on $R$. Put $J=(x_j:j\in\operatorname{Fin}(d))\subseteq P$ and $I=JR$. For an ideal $K\subseteq B$ write $B[t,K/t]$ for the subalgebra of $B[t,t^{-1}]$ generated by $B$, $t$, and $b t^{-1}$ for $b\in K$. Set $E=P[t,J/t]$ and $D=R[t,I/t]$. Coefficientwise extension of $\psi$ on Laurent polynomials restricts to $\eta:E\to D$. Define the following three canonical maps. The polynomial chart map $\chi:A[t][u_j:j\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)]\to D$ is the composite of $t\mapsto t$, $u_j\mapsto x_j/t$ into $E$ with $\eta$; it sends $a\in A$ to $\psi(a)$, $t$ to $t$, and $u_j$ to $\psi(x_j)/t$. The base map $\beta:A[t]\to A[t][u_j:j\in\operatorname{Fin}(d)]$ is the polynomial coefficient inclusion. The tensor map $\theta:R\otimes_P E\to D$, using the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with its standard commutative algebra structure, is the $R$-algebra map induced by the coefficient inclusion $R\to D$ and $\eta$; on pure tensors it is $r\otimes e\mapsto r\eta(e)$. These are definitions for every $\psi$; no flatness, etaleness, Noetherian or nonzero-ring hypothesis, and no bijectivity assertion, is part of this definition.
